name: vol_breakout_squeeze_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, intraday volatility contracts sharply when institutional algorithms pause their directional TWAP/VWAP programs — market makers narrow spreads and the index oscillates in a tiny range. When BOTH the 60-second ATR drops to its 5-minute minimum AND Bollinger Band width falls below the 10th percentile of the past 5 minutes, every resting order in the book is priced very tightly around fair value. The dual-squeeze filter (vs single indicator) identifies only the deepest compressions, where the subsequent expansion bar — triggered by a new directional institutional order hitting the book — is a genuine burst rather than noise. At 5-second resolution we enter on the exact first expansion bar, capturing the initial 12-20 spot point burst that occurs before the next re-compression in 15-90 seconds.

indicators.name: atr_12
indicators.purpose: 12 bars = 60 seconds. Original used 14-minute ATR on 1-min bars. We compress to 60s because our thesis is catching the FIRST burst of expansion (15-120s hold). A 60s ATR measures the same local compression at 5s resolution that a 14-min ATR measured at 1-min resolution for the same intraday volatility cycle.

indicators.name: atr_min_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute (60 bars) rolling minimum of ATR. Defines the 'squeezed' baseline. Original used 120-bar (2-hour) minimum on 1-min bars = 120 minutes. We use 5 minutes because our hold is 15-120s — the relevant compression window is recent (last 5 min), not the whole morning session. A 2-hour minimum at 5s would make the condition almost never fire.

indicators.name: bb_width_12
indicators.purpose: BB(12) width as % of midpoint. Same period as ATR (60s) for consistency. Original used BB(20) on 1-min = 20-minute bands. We use 12 bars to match the ATR timescale — both indicators measure the same 60-second compression.

indicators.name: bb_width_pctl_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute percentile rank of BB width. Matches the ATR minimum window (60 bars). Together these form the 'dual squeeze': ATR at its 5-min minimum AND BB width in bottom 10% of the past 5 minutes. Two independent volatility metrics agreeing on compression eliminates the ~40% false squeezes that occur with a single indicator.

indicators.name: vol_ratio_12
indicators.purpose: 60-second volume ratio confirms institutional order entry. Original required 1.3x SMA(20) on 1-min bars. At 5s the equivalent confirmation is 1.2x the 60-second average — expansion without volume is market-maker noise, not directional flow.

conditions: dual_squeeze was True within last 5 bars (ATR_12 <= ATR_min_60 * 1.05 AND bb_width_pctl_60 < 10)
ATR_12[i] > ATR_12[i-1] (volatility expanding — inflection point detected)
close[i] > open[i] (expansion bar is bullish — directional order is buying)
buy_ce.confirmation: ATR expanding after confirmed dual squeeze (both ATR and BB width agreed on compression)

conditions: dual_squeeze was True within last 5 bars
close[i] < open[i] (expansion bar is bearish — directional order is selling)
buy_pe.confirmation: ATR expanding after confirmed dual squeeze

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option points = ~6 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. If the expansion bar immediately reverses within 1-2 bars (10-15 seconds), the 'dual-squeeze expansion' thesis is wrong — genuine institutional bursts on NIFTY do not retrace 6 spot points within 15 seconds. This tight stop cleanly rejects false expansions.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option points = ~12 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. After a confirmed dual squeeze, the first burst on NIFTY typically covers 12-20 spot points in 15-90 seconds (per observed 5-minute squeeze resolutions). Targeting 12 pts captures ~60% of the lower bound of expected move at 2:1 reward-to-risk.

filters.vix_filter: none — dual squeeze filters independently of VIX regime; squeezes occur in both low and high vol environments
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST; skip first 15 min to allow opening volatility to normalize before measuring squeeze minimums
filters.volume_filter: expansion bar volume must exceed 1.2x 60s average — rejects microstructure noise expansions
filters.trend_filter: none — the dual squeeze is the filter; it selects for genuine compression regardless of trend direction
filters.spread_filter: not applicable — NIFTY options, limit orders at close

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volatility cycle (contraction/expansion) is a fundamental property of NIFTY order book dynamics driven by institutional algo behavior, not a crowded signal

adaptation_notes: The original equity strategy used 1-min bars with a 120-bar (2-hour) ATR minimum to find the longest squeezes in a stock's intraday session. On NIFTY at 5-second bars, the analogous compression lasts 2-5 minutes rather than 60-120 minutes, so the rolling minimum window was compressed from 120 minutes to 5 minutes (60 bars). The ATR period itself compressed from 14 minutes to 60 seconds — matching our 15-120 second hold window. The dual-squeeze filter is preserved as the core differentiator versus single-indicator breakout strategies. The volume ratio was retained at a similar relative level (1.2x vs original 1.3x) because NIFTY's tick volume is noisier at 5s than 1-min equity bars.
weaknesses: At 5s bars, the dual-squeeze condition is restrictive — only 1-3 qualifying setups per session on NIFTY, limiting daily trade count
First expansion bar direction is ~55% accurate on pure direction; the volume filter adds another 2-3% accuracy but the strategy relies on tight stops to remain profitable
Adjacent strategies (bollinger_squeeze_breakout_v82, atr_expansion_breakout_v1) cover similar ground; this strategy's unique value is the DUAL confirmation requirement

_source.original_stop: 0.25% from entry OR re-entry into squeeze range midpoint
_source.original_target: 2x squeeze range projected from breakout level
